cover.headline: [4] conversations that make her [want] you
cover.sub: (it starts long before the date ends)

picked.why: Flirty, playful expression with teasing energy matches attraction/connection messaging. Mysterious lakeside setting creates intrigue for 'conversations that make her want you'—inviting eye contact signals receptiveness.

slides: Skip the questions about her school or her job. Ask what the most trouble she got into as a kid was. It pulls her out of her serious grown-up mode and into a playful, rebellious mood. You're not talking to her resume. You're talking to her.
Ask what she secretly loves but is usually too embarrassed to admit. When she tells you, don't judge. Tease her, gently. It becomes a little secret that only the two of you share.

Tell her honestly what you thought the first time you saw her, and make it about her vibe, not just her face. Something like “I thought you looked like trouble.” She has to react, and it adds tension right away.

Bring up a trip you'd take together, and make it intense, not a boring beach week. “If we got stuck in a mountain cabin in a storm...” You're planting the picture of being alone with her somewhere exciting.
closing: Save this before your next first date.
caption:
4 conversations that build real attraction.

Ask about her childhood trouble. Ask her guilty pleasure and tease her. Tell her your honest first impression. Dream up an intense trip together.

Keep it light, read her reactions, and back off if she's not into it.

Which one will you try first?
